### About Multiplier Holdings

![Multiplier Holdings logo](https://seedtable.com/api/logo/own/0f49308e505d2614b937e4547897e452.png)

[Multiplier Holdings](https://seedtable.com/companies/multiplier-holdings)

[San Francisco](https://seedtable.com/best-startups-in-san-francisco), [United States](https://seedtable.com/best-startups-in-united-states)[Fintech](https://seedtable.com/best-fintech-startups)35.0M USD total raised [Website](https://multiplierholdings.com/)

Multiplier Holdings buys established professional services firms, tax and accounting practices in the first instance, and rebuilds their delivery around its own AI and workflow tooling, a roll-up strategy rather than a software sale. It launched publicly in June 2025 with $27.5 million across seed and Series A, the Series A led by Lightspeed Venture Partners and the seed by Ribbit Capital, and is run from San Francisco by former Stripe executive Noah Pepper.

### About This Round

[Multiplier Holdings](https://seedtable.com/companies/multiplier-holdings) raised a $35 million Series B announced on 4 August 2026, led by The General Partnership, with [Ribbit Capital](https://seedtable.com/investors/ribbit-capital) and existing investor [Lightspeed Venture Partners](https://seedtable.com/companies/lightspeed-venture-partners) participating.[1](https://www.dealstreetasia.com/stories/multiplier-funding-491273)

Founded by former Stripe executive Noah Pepper, Multiplier buys specialised professional-services firms - accounting and tax practices, mostly - and builds custom AI tools around how each one actually works. Acquired firms keep their brands, their leadership and their client relationships, and gain shared infrastructure and long-term capital. The company has bought eight firms so far, five of them in the past year, and has four more under signed term sheets.[1](https://www.dealstreetasia.com/stories/multiplier-funding-491273)

The round funds further acquisitions and expansion of the technology and operating teams. Multiplier has also appointed Allen Shim, formerly chief financial officer of Slack, as president and chief financial officer, covering finance, operations, partnerships and people, and leading the build-out of the San Francisco office. Clients now span more than ten countries.[2](https://itbrief.asia/story/multiplier-raises-usd-35-million-to-buy-specialist-firms)

This is a bet that the way to sell AI to accountants is to stop selling it to them. Software vendors have spent years discovering that professional-services firms buy slowly, pay little and change process reluctantly, which caps what a per-seat product can ever earn from the sector. Buying the firm instead converts a licence fee into the whole margin, and the automation shows up as operating leverage rather than as a line item someone has to justify. The hire is the clearest signal of what this company actually is: appointing a CFO as president says the constraint is capital allocation and integration, not product. Two things will decide it. The margin gain has to be durable rather than a one-off from digitising the obvious, and it has to stay proprietary - because if buying accounting firms and applying AI reliably expands margins, private equity can read that trade too, and it has far more money with which to bid up the same practices.
